profile_text.body:
The Technology Innovation Institute is a non-profit government research laboratory founded in 2020. Its site presents Falcon LLM as its generative large language model family, and describes the institute as the applied research pillar of Abu Dhabi's Advanced Technology Research Council (ATRC). The institute says its Falcon models are open source and frames the work as making advanced AI accessible and available to everyone, everywhere.

The Falcon family spans several models. Falcon-H1 and Falcon-E are described as the latest additions, with Falcon-H1 built on a hybrid Transformer and Mamba architecture. Falcon Perception is a multimodal model that combines vision and language so systems can read and understand images from natural language prompts. Falcon Arabic targets Modern Standard Arabic and dialects. Falcon H1R 7B is a 7B reasoning model for mathematics, coding, logic and instruction-following. Falcon Mamba 7B is described as the first open source released State Space Language Model. Earlier releases include Falcon 2 11B, Falcon 180B with 180 billion parameters trained on 3.5 trillion tokens, Falcon 40B with 40 billion parameters and one trillion tokens, and Falcon 10B. The site states that Falcon-H1 outperforms Meta's LLaMA and Alibaba's Qwen, and that Falcon 2 11B outperforms Meta's Llama 3 8B and performs on par with Google's Gemma 7B model, as independently verified by the Hugging Face Leaderboard.

The institute announced the Falcon Foundation, a non-profit dedicated to advancing open-source generative AI models and building ecosystems around open-source projects. AI71, described as an AI company launched by ATRC and VentureOne, issued a global call for proposals inviting developers to submit use cases for Falcon 10B, with the best proposals awarded compute access. The Falcon product tracked here is a UAE-hosted open-source LLM under an Apache 2.0 license, positioned around sovereign AI and Middle East data residency.
